title: Engineering Design: A Systematic Approach (3rd ed.)
actual_question: How to structure the design process systematically
theoretical_contribution: Canonical systematic design; abstraction/function structure precede embodiment (general knowledge of the method; book not accessed here)
relation_to_proposal: Function-before-embodiment sequencing is the textbook default

title: Development of a Functional Basis for Design
actual_question: Standard vocabulary for product function
theoretical_contribution: Functional basis in verb-object format; abstract: 'Functional models represent a form independent blueprint of a product'
relation_to_proposal: Formal machinery for describing the spoon as 'transfer food to mouth' already exists

title: A functional basis for engineering design: reconciling and evolving previous efforts
actual_question: Reconcile functional vocabularies
relation_to_proposal: Same as S02

title: The situated function-behaviour-structure framework
actual_question: Ontology of designing
theoretical_contribution: FBS: function, behaviour and structure are distinct and reformulated during design
relation_to_proposal: Already separates function from structure (form+material) and models reformulation

title: Design fixation
actual_question: Do example solutions constrain designers' concepts?
empirical_contribution: Example exposure increased feature repetition (classic finding; full text not read here, finding as reported in S14 abstract)
relation_to_proposal: Mechanism by which a familiar form could be retained is already named and measured
effect_on_originality: Removes novelty of 'form lock-in during ideation' as a mechanism

title: Design and other types of fixation
actual_question: Typology of fixation
theoretical_contribution: Links design fixation to problem-solving fixation
relation_to_proposal: Same mechanism family

title: Constraining effects of examples in a creative generation task
actual_question: Do examples constrain creative generation?
relation_to_proposal: Cognitive basis of conformity to familiar forms

title: Following the wrong footsteps: fixation effects of pictorial examples in a design problem-solving task
actual_question: Negative transfer from examples; can instructions defixate?
empirical_contribution: Two experiments (N=89; N=60): participants followed examples incl. flawed elements; defixating instructions reduced effect
relation_to_proposal: A framing instruction can change outcomes - the template for E3
effect_on_originality: Supports testability; reduces methodological originality of a framing manipulation

title: A study of design fixation, its mitigation and perception in engineering design faculty
actual_question: Are expert designers fixated, and can it be mitigated?
theoretical_contribution: Fixation persists in experts; mitigation possible
empirical_contribution: Control/fixation/defixation three-arm experiment with faculty; significant fixation, partially perceived
relation_to_proposal: Three-arm framing design already used; outcomes are fixation/novelty, not environmental
effect_on_originality: Reduces methodological originality; leaves environmental endpoint open

title: Design by analogy: a study of the WordTree method for problem re-representation
actual_question: Does functional re-representation of the problem widen search?
empirical_contribution: Controlled experiment: more analogies and out-of-domain search
relation_to_proposal: Function-verb re-representation is an existing tested intervention

title: A fix for fixation? Rerepresenting and abstracting as creative processes in the design of information systems
actual_question: Do abstraction and re-representation reduce fixation?
empirical_contribution: Both techniques yielded original ideas, but not all added ideas fit problem constraints
relation_to_proposal: Direct evidence that abstraction raises originality AND infeasibility: supports hostile objection on complexity/feasibility

title: Design fixation from initial examples: provided versus self-generated ideas
actual_question: Does fixation occur without a provided example?
empirical_contribution: Large experiment with beginning engineers: control group fixated on own first concept more than example group did
relation_to_proposal: A familiar form need not be supplied to fixate; complicates arm design in E3

title: Fixation and creativity in concept development: the attitudes and practices of expert designers
actual_question: How do professional designers view fixation?
empirical_contribution: 13 interviews; reports (citing Eckert et al. 2005) that reused prior work carries assumptions about physical properties, materials, processes and context
relation_to_proposal: Closest statement that inherited solutions import material/form assumptions
effect_on_originality: Reduces conceptual originality of 'inherited form/material assumptions'

title: Inspiration and fixation: questions, methods, findings, and challenges
actual_question: State of fixation research
empirical_contribution: Synthesises experiments; notes replication and measurement issues
relation_to_proposal: Defines the methodological standard E3 would have to meet

title: Where next for research on fixation, inspiration and creativity in design?
actual_question: Research agenda
theoretical_contribution: Questions whether measured feature repetition is always bad; calls for ecological validity
relation_to_proposal: Raises exactly the outcome-quality question (is fixation bad?) that an environmental endpoint would answer
effect_on_originality: Supports existence of an empirical gap (outcome quality, not novelty)

title: Influence of environmental information on creativity
actual_question: Does environmental information affect designers' creativity? (from title)
empirical_contribution: Findings NOT verified (abstract and full text unavailable; Unpaywall: closed; S2: no abstract)
relation_to_proposal: Closest experimental precedent linking environmental framing and ideation; its findings must be read before any E3

title: Evolution of design for sustainability: from product design to design for system innovations and transitions
actual_question: How has DfS evolved?
theoretical_contribution: Four-level framework: product, product-service system, spatio-social, socio-technical system
empirical_contribution: Literature synthesis; reports early green design focused on redesigning individual qualities of products (e.g. replacing virgin with recycled, hazardous with non-hazardous materials); PSS defined as delivering functions instead of products; calls to move beyond product improvements alone
relation_to_proposal: Ecodesign already names material-level improvement as the earliest, narrowest level and already argues to move beyond product form

title: Ecodesign: A Promising Approach to Sustainable Production and Consumption
doi_or_stable_id: ISBN not verified; reference verified in S17 reference list
actual_question: Ecodesign method
theoretical_contribution: Commonly associated with the product improvement / redesign / function innovation / system innovation levels - NOT verified from source in this gate
relation_to_proposal: If the commonly cited four-level model is confirmed, it is the closest conceptual precedent
effect_on_originality: Likely decisive against conceptual novelty; verification pending

title: Mapping the green product development field: engineering, policy and business perspectives
actual_question: Map of green product development literature
relation_to_proposal: Relevant to whether material-focused practice dominates

title: Clarifying the concept of product-service system
actual_question: Definition of PSS
relation_to_proposal: 'Delivery system' reopening is PSS

title: Eight types of product-service system: eight ways to sustainability?
actual_question: Are PSS types environmentally better?
empirical_contribution: SusProNet evaluation: eight PSS types with diverging environmental characteristics; 'most PSS types will result in marginal environmental improvements at best', exception 'functional results' type (abstract)
relation_to_proposal: Shows function-delivery reframing is not automatically better

title: Product/service-systems for a circular economy: the route to decoupling economic growth from resource consumption?
actual_question: Conditions under which PSS yields absolute decoupling
theoretical_contribution: Two-step framework; PSS no implicit guarantee
relation_to_proposal: Reopening delivery system does not guarantee lower impact

authors: Bocken, de Pauw, Bakker, van der Grinten
title: Product design and business model strategies for a circular economy
actual_question: Design and business-model strategies for circularity
relation_to_proposal: Strategy space already extends far beyond material substitution

title: Product design in a circular economy: development of a typology of key concepts and terms
actual_question: Typology of circular design
relation_to_proposal: Same

title: Towards a sufficiency-driven business model
actual_question: Sufficiency business models
relation_to_proposal: 'Do we need the spoon at all?' is sufficiency

title: Integration of sustainability into early design through the function impact matrix
actual_question: How to bring LCA into function-oriented early design
theoretical_contribution: Function Impact Matrix combining LCA with functional-component matrix, QFD, Pugh
relation_to_proposal: Function-level environmental assessment during conceptual design already exists
effect_on_originality: Strongly reduces originality of 'function-first environmental decision method'

title: Development of an eco-ideation tool to identify stepwise greenhouse gas emissions reduction options for consumer goods
actual_question: Eco-ideation tool
relation_to_proposal: Ideation tool targeting GHG reduction options

title: Where do professionals find sustainability and innovation value? Empirical tests of three sustainable design methods
actual_question: Which components of sustainable design methods do professionals value?
empirical_contribution: 23 workshops, >172 professionals, 27 companies; value measured by self-report because objectively assessing many vague early-stage ideas for sustainability was 'deemed too subjective and too highly uncertain'
relation_to_proposal: Closest empirical comparison of design methods for sustainability; explicitly did NOT measure environmental performance of outcomes
effect_on_originality: Confirms empirical gap AND documents the main feasibility barrier for E3

authors: Faludi, Hoffenson, Kwok, Saidani et al.
title: A research roadmap for sustainable design methods and tools
actual_question: Research needs for sustainable design methods
relation_to_proposal: Calls for empirically grounded methods; positions the gap
effect_on_originality: Supports gap; not prior empirical answer

title: Adopting and applying eco-design techniques: a practitioners perspective
actual_question: Applicability of eco-design techniques in NPD
empirical_contribution: Single product case (chemical detector) using checklists/guidelines/MET matrix
relation_to_proposal: Practice evidence of what ecodesign actually does in firms
effect_on_originality: Neutral; one case cannot establish substitution bias

title: Ecodesign tools for designers: defining the requirements
actual_question: Requirements of industrial designers for ecodesign tools
relation_to_proposal: Practice context

title: Specifying functional units and reference flows for comparable alternatives
actual_question: How to define functional units for comparing alternatives
relation_to_proposal: LCA already requires function-defined comparison across alternatives
effect_on_originality: Strongly reduces originality of 'function as requirement' in assessment

title: System boundaries and input data in consequential life cycle inventory analysis
actual_question: Consequential LCI
relation_to_proposal: Needed for any claim that redesign changes system outcomes

title: Toward substitution with no regrets
actual_question: Avoiding regrettable chemical substitution
relation_to_proposal: Burden shifting from like-for-like substitution is already recognised (chemicals)

title: Environmental impacts of takeaway food containers
actual_question: LCA of aluminium, PP, EPS and reusable PP containers
empirical_contribution: EPS single-use had lowest impacts; reusable PP better only after 3-39 reuses
relation_to_proposal: Material intuitions can be wrong; reuse (delivery-system change) is conditional
effect_on_originality: Shows environmental endpoint cannot be assumed

title: Plastic or glass: a new environmental assessment with a marine litter indicator for the comparison of pasteurized milk bottles
actual_question: PET/R-PET vs glass/returnable glass
empirical_contribution: LCA: R-PET bottle lowest on several categories (abstract)
relation_to_proposal: Material substitution assumptions contradicted case-specifically

title: Don't scrap the waste: the need for broader system boundaries in bioplastic food packaging life-cycle assessment
actual_question: Do bioplastic packaging LCAs capture food-waste trade-offs?
empirical_contribution: 19 LCAs: conflicting picture; benefits for GWP often negated by agricultural inputs; food protection function must be included
relation_to_proposal: Exactly the 'material substitution evaluated without the function' critique, already published

title: Environmental sustainability of liquid food packaging: is there a gap between Danish consumers' perception and learnings from LCA?
actual_question: Do consumer perceptions match LCA?
empirical_contribution: Survey+interviews: consumers judge mainly by material type and own disposal; compared with streamlined LCA
relation_to_proposal: Material-centred judgement demonstrated for CONSUMERS, not designers
effect_on_originality: Partial support for a 'material heuristic' premise (demand side only)

title: Paper meets plastic: the perceived environmental friendliness of product packaging
actual_question: Do consumers misjudge packaging greenness?
theoretical_contribution: PEF bias; 'paper = good, plastic = bad' lay belief
empirical_contribution: Eight studies (N=4,103): plastic+paper judged greener than identical plastic; affects WTP/choice; minimal-packaging sticker mitigates
relation_to_proposal: Strongest evidence that material labels drive environmental judgement - on the consumer side
effect_on_originality: Supports a premise; also shows the bias topic is already published

title: Environmental taxation of plastic bags and substitutes: balancing marine pollution and climate change
actual_question: Optimal taxation when bans induce substitution
relation_to_proposal: Policy-induced like-for-like substitution and trade-offs already modelled

title: Understanding carbon lock-in
actual_question: Why carbon-intensive systems persist
relation_to_proposal: Lock-in of dominant designs is established theory

title: Competing technologies, increasing returns, and lock-in by historical events
actual_question: Path dependence in technology adoption
empirical_contribution: Not assessed (OpenAlex abstract field contains only citation text)
